title: Strategy and Observer
summary: Swap algorithms at runtime; notify without knowing who listens.

cards.title: Strategy: same call, different algorithm
cards.body: A `PayRule` interface with two implementations. The code that settles a spin never changes when designers switch pay models.
Lighter alternative in modern C++: a `std::function` holding a lambda. Use an interface when the strategy has several methods or its own state.

cards.title: Observer, recap
cards.body:
The Lambda Lab's callbacks are the Observer pattern: the subject keeps a list of `std::function` listeners and calls them on events. Sound, UI and analytics react to "win" without the game logic knowing they exist.

Watch out: a listener that captured `this` by reference must be removed before that object dies, or the callback dangles.

cards.question: Which change does Strategy make easy?
choices: Adding a new pay model without editing the settle code
cards.explain: New behaviour arrives as a new class (or lambda) behind the same interface. The calling code stays untouched: the Open/Closed principle.
